title: Quarterly Alignment Lab + Renewal Scenario Scripts
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is an engineer-friendly, scenario-driven QBR facilitation lab intended to train CS teams and to be reused as a meeting script and preflight checklist for accounts approaching renewal windows. It’s intentionally conversational — use the short scripts as starting lines and adapt to voice-of-customer.

When to use this doc:
- Mid-market accounts with 6+ months of usage and upcoming renewal within 90 days.
- Strategic expansion accounts where we expect cross-sell conversations.
- Any QBR where risk signals (usage drop, feature regression, exec churn) are present.

High-level meeting flow (90 minutes template)
1) 0:00–0:07 — Kick / context-setting (CS lead)
   - Quick intros (name, role, one-sentence success metric)
   - State meeting objective: align goals, surface risks, agree on next-steps for renewal or expansion
   - Confirm time and priority topics from customer (ask: anything to add to the top 3?)

2) 0:07–0:25 — Health snapshot & trend beats (CS analyst)
   - Replace slides with 2 screens: adoption trends (weekly active routes), cost-per-token trends, latency SLOs, error %
   - Script: "Over the last 90 days we saw X% growth in routable requests, but latency for long-form generation increased by Yms — that correlates with the change to batch policy on Dec 14."

3) 0:25–0:40 — Outcomes review (customer / champion)
   - Ask the customer to speak to business outcomes: product metrics improved? time-to-resolution saved? revenue signals?
   - Script prompts: "Which of these results mattered most to your stakeholders? Where did you expect more impact?"

4) 0:40–0:60 — Risk & friction lab (facilitated discussion + scenario roleplay)
   - Present two micro-scenarios (Quality regression, Capacity constraint) and walk through fallbacks.
   - Scenario 1 (Quality regression): "Imagine we release an embedding model variant that reduces semantic drift but introduces edge-case hallucinations in legal docs. How would you like us to surface these regressions and roll back?"
   - Scenario 2 (Capacity spike): "You plan a marketing event that will triple inference traffic for 48 hours. If Dedicated capacity isn’t available, which of these fallback policies should we trigger? (a) degrade to a cheaper model, (b) queue requests with progress streaming, (c) provision burst GPUs)"
   - Use the heatmap matrix (risk x impact x owner) — capture decisions live.

5) 0:60–0:80 — Renewal & commercial runway (CS lead + AE)
   - Capture renewal timing and discuss license shape: committed tokens vs. pay-as-you-go, burst add-ons, SLA uplift
   - Script: "Given your growth plan of X%%, our recommendation is a modest reserved capacity commit to hold latency SLOs during peak campaigns; this reduces unit cost by Y%% and buys priority scheduling."

6) 0:80–0:90 — Commitments & next steps (all)
   - Confirm action owners, deadlines, and up-next check-ins.
   - Quick pulse: each attendee says one sentence: I’m confident / I need follow-up / Concern flagged.

Preflight checklist (48–72 hours before)
- Confirm attendee list with exec and technical champion; require decision-maker on renewal or procurement on call when possible.
- Upload metrics snapshot to shared folder (last 90 days): WAU, requests/day, p50/p95 latency, error %, token spend.
- Verify model versions in production and note any model switchover dates in last quarter.
- Run a short smoke test of critical routes (3 representative prompts) and paste outputs into the doc for live review.
- Prepare two tailored scenarios for the customer (one growth, one risk) and one recommended commercial path.
- Coordinate with AE on renewal posture; align on negotiation guardrails and discount bands.
- Pre-seed slide or Google doc with suggested commitments and optional add-ons to speed decision making.

Facilitation scripts (short, adaptable lines)
- Opening: "Thanks for joining — our goal today is simple: make sure we’re delivering on the outcomes you care about and make a clear recommendation for the upcoming renewal window."
- When customer is quiet: "We have x minutes — can you help us prioritize the top two outcomes we should be measuring next quarter?"
- On hearing a complaint: "That’s helpful feedback. Can you share an example of where that cost/latency hit a customer or internal stakeholder?"
- When steering to renewal: "We want to propose a plan that keeps you covered during your big events and reduces per-token cost; would you prefer a 12-month reserved option or a 6-month with burst credits?"
- Closing: "We’ll capture action items now and share a one-page decision memo by EOD tomorrow with owners and dates."

Scenario lab examples (templates you can edit)
- Expansion win: Marketing Bot launch. Inputs: traffic forecast x3, peak burst, strict latency p95 < 700ms. Options: temporary Dedicated burst + caching + lighter model for non-critical routes. Expected outcome: preserve critical flows, avoid overprovisioning costs.
- Compliance trigger: New regulatory requirement forces audited logs and HSM-based key storage for prompts. Ask: timeline, certification owner, migration window. Recommended: Private deployment pilot + staged rollout.
- Quality regression: New model reduces hallucinations for 80% of cases but increases hallucinations on niche prompts. Mitigation: small canary, A/B test with sampling, rollback plan and prompt set for automated quality alarms.

Decision capture template (use in doc during meeting)
- Decision: short text
- Owner: name
- Target date: date
- Acceptance criteria: short bullet list
- Contingency: short text
(Keep a running table at the bottom of the meeting doc — copy/paste into CRM post-meeting)

Post-meeting deliverables (24–72 hours)
- One-page decision memo (1–2 bullets per decision) — share to execs and procurement.
- Action tracker exported to shared spreadsheet and linked to opportunity in CRM.
- Health check rebaseline: update trend charts with the smoke test results and publish to drive.
- Renewal proposal draft (AE): include the recommended commit, pricing, and technical add-ons; CS to validate capacity assumptions.

Notes on tone and moderation
- Aim for curiosity-first questioning; use data to anchor claims and avoid pricing-first language until alignment achieved.
- Call out unknowns explicitly and promise concrete next steps for any open items.
- Keep the meeting timeboxed; when tangents arise, capture them as separate action items.

Appendix — quick reference snippets for sticky situations
- If procurement requests immediate 20% discount: "We can consider that for a 24-month committed arrangement; for a 12-month commit we can do X% and include Y credits for burst."
- If exec is skeptical of ROI: "Here are three quick metrics your execs care about — cost per resolved ticket, time-to-first-value (days), and revenue retention attributable to the feature — which should we include in the renewal brief?"
- If technical churn: "We’ll schedule a technical deep-dive within 7 business days to map dependencies, and we’ll place temporary monitoring alerts on any routes you mark fragile."

Usage guidance and maintenance
- Keep this doc as the living facilitation lab. After each QBR, CS lead should append 2 lines: what worked / what to change. Update scenarios quarterly to reflect product launches or new risk patterns.
- Tag the doc with the account name and copy into the opportunity folder in GDrive.

Quick edit log (example)
- 2025-01-18: Initial draft by Ava Morales (scenario templates + 90-min flow).
- 2025-01-24: Added preflight checklist and technical smoke-test prompts (Diego Patel).
- 2025-02-02: Aligned commercial scripting with AE guidance, added procurement snippets (Renee Park).

End of doc.
